page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 192 vCPUs derived from 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled running at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 720.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in multi-core processing, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier for both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the middle tier and Geekbench single-core in the top quarter. The server demonstrates top-tier capabilities in specialized tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, text processing, and cryptography, aided by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

Given its high core density and dedicated resource allocation, the server offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that can leverage its massive multi-threaded capacity and memory bandwidth without requiring local SSDs or GPUs. It is suited for large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, database operations, and CPU-based LLM inference, where it achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds on medium and large models.
